correctness.rationale: The initial independence and domination requirements force consecutive selected vertices on a simple cycle of length at least six to be separated by two or three edges. An exhaustive local swap analysis proves the necessary/sufficient two-short-gap separation, leading to a bijection with disjoint two-vertex/one-selected blocks and seven-vertex/three-selected blocks. Double-counting labelled block origins gives the exact n/(a+b) binomial coefficient. Simple-cycle exceptions of lengths 3, 4, 5 are treated directly. The logarithmic derivative and coprime length argument yield the dominant-root asymptotic. A separately coded exhaustive direct-neighbor-swap checker verified every subset, each gap rule, and all coefficients for 4 <= n <= 22. Finite checking is supplementary; the local argument handles all n. Post-swap independence is intentionally NOT imposed.

value.rationale: Independent secure domination is an independently motivated guard-protection invariant with previously established minimum cycle sizes. Counting ALL feasible labelled configurations is not implied by the minimum: the exact two/seven cyclic tiling law determines every size coefficient and shows exponential scarcity versus ordinary independent domination. This explains structural robustness and permits exact probabilistic deployment/reliability questions on arbitrarily large rings. The pentagon absence and the growing number of nonminimum configurations are natural, substantive features rather than arbitrary finite slices.
